Similarly, duplicate detection against existing attendees uses `guest === attendee.email` without lowercasing. An attacker can bypass the blacklist by using mixed-case emails (e.g., `Blocked@example.com`) and may create duplicate attendees when an existing attendee's email differs only by case. findings.title: Team admins are denied permission due to && instead of ||
findings.body: The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires the user to be both team admin and team owner simultaneously, which effectively excludes team admins who are not owners. As a result, team admins cannot add guests to team event bookings even though they should have permission, causing a 403 FORBIDDEN error on a valid action.

findings.title: Case-sensitive email comparison bypasses blacklist and duplicate detection
findings.body: The blacklist emails are lowercased, but the input guest emails are not normalized before comparison (`blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Similarly, duplicate detection against existing attendees uses `guest === attendee.email` without lowercasing. An attacker can bypass the blacklist by using mixed-case emails (e.g., `Blocked@example.com`) and may create duplicate attendees when an existing attendee's email differs only by case. This can lead to unwanted calendar invitations and data integrity issues.

findings.title: Calendar update uses acting user's credentials instead of organizer's
findings.body: The handler builds the EventManager with `ctx.user` and credentials fetched from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`, ignoring the booking's actual organizer stored in `booking.user` (which includes `credentials` and `destinationCalendar`). If the person adding guests is a team admin or a different attendee, calendar invitations are sent/updated using that user's calendar integration, not the organizer's. This can fail to update the correct calendar, send invites from the wrong email, or expose the acting user's calendar credentials to the event.

findings.title: No seats capacity check before adding guests
findings.body: For bookings with limited seats (`seatsPerTimeSlot`), the handler does not check whether adding new guests would exceed the allowed number of attendees. Users can add unlimited guests beyond the configured seat limit, leading to over-capacity bookings and inconsistent data between the booking and event type capacity.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails uses original input list instead of actually added guests
findings.body: The function receives `newGuests` as the original `guests` array from the input, not the filtered `uniqueGuests` that were actually added. If the input contained an existing attendee's email (duplicate) or a blacklisted email, that email will still appear in `newGuests`. For existing attendees, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` will be true, causing them to receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (a new booking confirmation) instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. This can confuse users and duplicate confirmation emails. The function should instead receive the list of emails that were actually added (`uniqueGuests`).

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore event-type email disable settings
findings.body: Other email sending functions in this file check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` from the event type metadata and skip sending if disabled. `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept or check these flags, so organizer/attendee emails are sent even for event types where standard emails are disabled. This violates user preferences and may send unwanted notifications.

findings.title: Error toast shows raw TRPC code and may not fallback to default message
findings.body: The error handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then does `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. If `err.data?.code` is undefined, the message becomes `undefined: <translation>`, which is truthy, so the fallback is never used. Additionally, `err.data?.code` is a TRPC error code like `BAD_REQUEST` or `FORBIDDEN`, not a user-facing message, and concatenating it with a colon produces output like "BAD_REQUEST: Emails must be unique and valid". The toast should display a friendly error, not the internal code.
